applicable_when: The kernel has xnumel=9 but XBLOCK=128, meaning 119 of 128 threads per block are masked idle on the X dimension — a ~93% thread waste per block. The grid is (1, 1024) = 1024 blocks on 132 SMs, giving only 0.48 waves/SM. Half the SMs receive no work. Achieved occupancy is 34.9% vs 100% theoretical. The fix is to set XBLOCK=1 so threads are not wasted on masked X lanes, and increase YBLOCK (e.g. 128-512) to pack more useful work per CTA and improve SM utilization. Adding @triton.autotune lets the runtime find the best combination automatically.

applicable_when: The kernel has xnumel=9 but XBLOCK=128, meaning 119 out of 128 threads per block are masked out and do zero work — a 93% thread waste. The grid is (cdiv(9,128)=1, cdiv(8192,8)=1024) = 1024 total blocks on 132 SMs = 0.48 waves. Achieved occupancy is only 34.9% vs 100% theoretical. The fix is to autotune with XBLOCK=1 (or small values) so the x-dimension is handled efficiently, and increase YBLOCK to pack more real work per block. With XBLOCK=1 and YBLOCK=128, the grid becomes (9, 64) = 576 blocks — 4.36 waves — and every thread does real work.
